gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Cheerful and loud, Luckiest Guy draws marker-like lines at a constant width. Noto Sans Soyombo follows with a sizable x-height and curves that stay open, so a long page would read smoothly on screen.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-sundanese: Noto Sans Sundanese reads clean and tight, with barely any gap between its lowercase and capitals. Luckiest Guy is the one for tube-like punch that holds through every bend, and the sans handles the quiet, steady lines.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Fat, poured-ink letters with a mean line set high, and an e that opens clearly to the right in Luckiest Guy. Noto Sans Sunuwar settles in beneath it, its curves leaving daylight, so a longer page goes down easily.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nag: Every stroke in Luckiest Guy ends at the same measured thickness, which gives it its loud, cheerful bluntness. And Noto Syloti Nagri's tall x-height and short ascenders make the quieter half of the pairing.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-syriac: Thin steel rod, bent into loud letters. Luckiest Guy sets that against Noto Sans Syriac, whose blown-glass bowls and wide, easy s shapes keep the page friendly and modern underneath the shouting.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-syriac-eas: Luckiest Guy has the steady line of a technical drafting pen, cheerful and loud with a high, mean brow. Noto Sans Syriac Eastern keeps its tall lowercase and curve endings apart for quiet reading.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-syriac-wes: Noto Sans Syriac Western reads modern and clean, its small letters thick with height like bundled cable. And Luckiest Guy needs no hairlines at all, so give the sans-serif body a little extra size to hold its own.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Luckiest Guy brings true monoline drawing and a loud, cheerful grin, with the e opening clearly to the right. And Noto Sans Tagalog supplies the strongest quality of the pair: a middle-heavy texture with generous curve gaps.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Cheerful, with diagonals as thick as its horizontals, Luckiest Guy shouts first. Noto Sans Tagbanwa answers in lowercase that fills most of the height, its open curves giving the loud heading a friendly, readable partner.
gen-luckiest-guy-gf-noto-sans-tai-le: Luckiest Guy keeps one stroke thickness everywhere, pouring loud, cheerful ink under a mean high line. Noto Sans Tai Le takes the opposite job, tapering its strokes out before they touch and keeping the cap-to-lowercase step minimal.
